findings.text: follow-on: the exited-unfinished action string hardcodes --status complete, but the state fires precisely when no verdict word was written and the run may equally have exhausted or failed; the suggested remediation nudges the coordinator toward a complete verdict for a run the evidence does not show completed.

follow-on: the hook declares its own WAITING_STATUS = "waiting" while reckon/crew/recovery.py:99 owns the same vocabulary and the hook already imports _manifest_wait from that module at line 44, so a rename on either side would leave the module-level status check silently testing the wrong word.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit — b88a904a9 (feature: recovery state, runs repair, cli verb, hook wait, ticker palette, watch vocabulary, five tests), 3896a49ab (help-census row and count), 5a5918d18 (format fold), all inside scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when requires one test per defect failing before the change, each naming its own reproduction, and the manifest records the base and head arms — base 5 failed at tests/test_run_state_reads_what_the_worker_reached.py and tests/test_crew_help_names_its_state.py, head 1 failed at the later id.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is defects 1 and 2 of plan crew-observability-truth section 26 — give a run whose recorded exit left an open manifest status its own state, provide a sanctioned status repair, and let the worker stop hook accept a well-formed status waiting; reckon/crew/recovery.py:6342 and reckon/hooks/worker_stop.py:236 carry both.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it states the arms, the negative control and the ruff delta, and its baseline_suite and after_suite blocks name the gate logs that the logs themselves reproduce.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's seven declared paths; the diff over 53a72f8c..5a5918d18 shows every changed file inside them and the worktree clean at head.

justifications.durability: the five new assertions each fail on the code change they guard (the negative control reverted waiting acceptance and tests/test_run_state_reads_what_the_worker_reached.py:243 reddened), and none compares a value against the same variable the test passed in; docked because no test pins the boundary the docstring claims — that a killed worker with no exit record stays interrupted, and that exited-unfinished does not fire with zero commits beyond base.
justifications.evidence: gate-base.log reads 5 failed, 539 passed and gate-head-2.log 1 failed, 544 passed, the head failure id is one of the base five so no failure id is added, the negative control negative-control-2.log is EXIT=1 with the waiting case failing, and I re-ran tests/test_run_state_reads_what_the_worker_reached.py at head (5 passed in 2.11s) — recorded, not claimed.
justifications.fit: the state is mechanism-named and wired through the existing RECOVERY_CLASSES, RECOVERY_VERBS, NEEDS_ACTION and WATCH_ATTENTION_STATES sets rather than a parallel path, and the hook reads the classifier's own wait reader; docked because reckon/hooks/worker_stop.py:43 duplicates the WAITING_STATUS literal that reckon/crew/recovery.py:99 already owns rather than importing it beside the _manifest_wait import it already makes.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/recovery.py:6339 emits a recognised exited-unfinished state with a repair verb and action, reckon/cli.py:5417 adds crew repair-status keeping manifest.md.asdelivered (reckon/crew/runs.py:1103), and reckon/hooks/worker_stop.py:227 accepts a waiting manifest whose wait block _manifest_wait honours — both defects reproduced and repaired, docked for the action hardcoding --status complete at recovery.py:6353.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in 53a72f8c..5a5918d18 (reckon/cli.py, reckon/crew/recovery.py, reckon/crew/runs.py, reckon/crew/ticker.py, reckon/hooks/worker_stop.py, tests/test_run_state_reads_what_the_worker_reached.py, tests/test_crew_help_names_its_state.py) is inside the manifest's declared write paths, and the census count 34 to 35 matches the repair-status row it added.
